question: What is the main goal of giving critical care right in the community?

options.A: To completely replace big hospital intensive care units
options.B: To perform minor surgeries in local health posts
options.C: To keep the patient alive and protect vital organs before getting them to a hospital
options.D: To provide long-term care for lifestyle diseases

explanation: Community critical care focuses on stabilizing patients immediately to prevent death during the crucial period before reaching a large hospital. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why is emergency care in the community especially important within the Nigerian health system?

options.A: Primary health centers have plenty of specialist doctors
options.B: Big tertiary hospitals are usually far away and take a long time to reach
options.C: Rural health posts are packed with advanced ventilators
options.D: People at home always reject going to modern hospitals

explanation: Long travel distances and bad roads mean that giving care right at the primary level is essential to keep patients alive before a long trip. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h1)

question: What usually causes patients to arrive at a primary health center in a severe, life-threatening stage?

options.A: Having too many intensive care beds available
options.B: Waiting too long before seeking medical help due to money or travel problems
options.C: Depending too much on routine immunization programs
options.D: Coming in too early for simple coughs

explanation: Financial and distance barriers often cause people to delay coming to the clinic, making their illnesses much worse by the time they arrive. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h2)

question: What kinds of health emergencies do nurses usually see in community settings?

options.B: No injuries or accidents at all
options.C: Only mild cases of dehydration and shock
options.D: A mix of severe infectious diseases and rising chronic emergencies

explanation: Communities deal with both infectious illnesses and non-communicable emergencies like high blood pressure strokes and accidents. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h2)

question: In the standard emergency ABCDE assessment, what does the letter 'C' stand for?
explanation: In emergency checks, C stands for circulation, which means assessing pulses, blood flow, and blood pressure. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h3)

question: A patient is brought to the clinic, does not answer when called, but groans when pinched. Which triage level fits best?

options.A: Delayed care suitable for health talks
options.B: Non-urgent case for home care advice

explanation: An altered level of consciousness where the patient only responds to pain is a serious sign requiring immediate medical action. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h3)

question: What is the best initial position for an unconscious patient who is breathing and has no injuries?

options.C: Flat on their back with legs straight

explanation: The recovery position keeps the airway open by stopping the tongue from blocking the throat and letting saliva drain out. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why must intravenous fluids be given and watched very carefully during community resuscitation?

options.A: Without advanced monitors, giving too much fluid can easily overload the heart and lungs
options.B: Patients usually refuse drips because of cultural beliefs
options.C: IV fluids do not work at all for shock
options.D: Infusion sets react badly with local water

explanation: Without central line monitors, running too much fluid too fast can cause fluid to back up into the lungs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the standard medicine used to stop active eclamptic seizures in a primary clinic?
explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice to treat and prevent further seizures in severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h5)

question: A patient arrives struggling to breathe, wheezing loudly, and using neck muscles to draw air in. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Give bronchodilators and check oxygen levels
options.C: Send them home with cough syrup
options.D: Prepare the patient for immediate surgery

explanation: Sudden airway tightening needs quick airway help and bronchodilators to ease breathing difficulties. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the most important rule when a nurse has to improvise medical tools in a rural clinic?

options.A: Wait for official supplies from the city before helping
options.B: Never compromise basic sterile technique and patient safety
options.C: Always use heavy metal objects to make things strong
options.D: Never write down improvised methods in the notes

explanation: Improvising must never introduce germs or dangers that could hurt the patient more. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h6)

question: Which of these is a very common challenge in rural health centers?

options.A: Unsteady electricity and shortages of basic equipment
options.B: An excess of intensive care specialists
options.C: Computers with fast telemedicine in every room

explanation: Power cuts and a lack of manufactured medical supplies are everyday hurdles in rural health facilities. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h6)

question: What vital paper must go along with a very sick patient being transferred to a big hospital?

options.A: A financial receipt for clinic registration
options.D: A detailed referral letter showing findings and treatments given

explanation: A complete referral note helps receiving nurses know what happened, what treatments were given, and what the patient still needs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h7)

question: Why is it important for a trained nurse to ride along with a critical patient during transport?

options.A: To argue about hospital admission fees at the gate
options.B: To drive the ambulance if the driver gets tired
options.C: To draw blood for lab tests while traveling
options.D: To watch vital signs and handle sudden changes on the way

explanation: Patients can easily get worse on rough roads, needing constant observation and quick nursing care. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h7)

question: What is the main focus of palliative care for terminally ill patients in the community?

options.B: Keeping the patient on a machine at all costs
options.C: Aggressive surgery to cure failing organs
options.D: Pain relief, symptom control, and emotional comfort

explanation: Palliative care puts quality of life, comfort, and dignity first when a cure is no longer possible. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h8)

question: What is the best approach when caring for a terminally ill patient at home?

options.A: Avoid talking about their illness with the family
options.B: Withhold all drugs so they do not get addicted
options.C: Support family members and manage distressing symptoms with compassion
options.D: Insist on moving them to a busy intensive care unit

explanation: Home palliative care centers on easing physical pain and supporting the emotional needs of both patient and family. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h8)

question: Who do community nurses often work closely with to handle local health emergencies?

options.A: Community health extension workers and local leaders

explanation: Primary healthcare works best through teamwork involving nurses, health extension workers, and community leaders. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h9)

question: How does combining public health with clinical care help communities handle emergencies better?

options.A: By turning every primary clinic into a giant hospital
options.B: By removing the need for community health nurses entirely
options.C: By combining emergency response with disease prevention and monitoring
options.D: By focusing only on private city surgical centers

explanation: Pairing clinical care with public health measures helps prevent health crises before they erupt while keeping emergency readiness strong. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h9)
